free_tier.stated: three hosted runner labels on a free Codeberg account, in open alpha: tiny, small and medium. No job-count cap and no monthly minute meter is published; the only published ceiling is the per-job runtime of 2, 5 or 10 minutes

per_object_cap.stated: codeberg-tiny 1 CPU / 2 GB / 2 min; codeberg-small 2 CPU / 4 GB / 5 min; codeberg-medium 4 CPU / 8 GB / 10 min
per_object_cap.notes: the RAM allocation includes writes to the filesystem, with 2 GB of extra temporary storage per container

retention.stated: no artifact retention is published; the service is in open alpha

interface_detail: a GitHub-Actions-compatible workflow with runs-on set to a codeberg label; the default image is ghcr.io/catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest
tooling: the act-compatible image; podman for image builds; no Docker daemon
chaining: a GitHub-Actions-compatible workflow on a free runner for jobs that finish in ten minutes, which is the only free path to Actions syntax without a GitHub repository

limits.value: 2 minutes per job on tiny, 5 on small, 10 on medium
1, 2 and 4 CPUs, with 2, 4 and 8 GB of RAM, and the RAM includes filesystem writes
lazy variants exist and may wait up to 24 hours for a slot

reliability_note: open alpha: the runner sizes are guidelines enforced by fair use rather than hard quotas, and the CI page states the service 'might break at any time and for an undefined period of time'
confidence_note: the runner table was read from Codeberg's own meta repository.

evidence.proved: 'codeberg-tiny amd64 1 2G 2 min'; 'codeberg-small amd64 2 4G 5 min'; 'codeberg-medium amd64 4 8G 10 min'; 'The RAM allocation includes writes to the filesystem ... we grant you 2 GB of additional storage for temporary files per container'; the lazy variants may take up to 24 hours
Forgejo Actions is available with self-hosted runners and a hosted version in limited fashion in open alpha

notes: Ten minutes on four CPUs is 40 CPU-minutes per job, and the jobs are unlimited. That is a real free compute lane for short work and it is the only one here with no monthly meter.
